newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity finishes strong on physicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity finishes strong on physicals.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures continued to uncover new contract highs Friday as strong physicals helped the front-month contracts finish the week much higher, industry sources said.

NYMEX July Palo Verde (PV) futures ended up $2.03 at $33.40 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new high of $33.75. August settled $1.40 higher at the contract high of $34.20 per MWh. Other front months were 99 cents to $1.60 higher.

July California-Oregon Border (COB) settled at $24.44, up $1.04, after reaching another new contract high of $24.75. August at the close was up 66 cents at $26.65 after hovering between $25.60 and $26.75 per MWh. Other months were 10-55 cents firmer.

"Pre-scheduled prices are continuing to pull it higher in the Southwest, and that's filtering into COB too," one Northwest source said, noting the plant outages were also lending support to the market.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 912 COB and 910 PV contracts traded.
Physical power prices in the U.S. Southwest remained strong, sources said, with Monday peak, firm PV power assessed at $45.00-49.00 from Thursday's discussion at $40.00-42.00 per MWh.
Monday peak, firm COB power was pegged near $32.00 per MWh early, though sources said prices by early afternoon had returned near Thursday's levels at $27.00-30.00.

Weather in the U.S. Southwest continued to be the major factor driving cash and futures higher, traders said. However, the exceptions were southern California and the mountains of Nevada, Utah and Colorado, where rains pushed temperatures back near normal.
Phoenix, Ariz., continued to rank at the top of the list as temperature highs were expected to reach 107 degrees Fahrenheit on Saturday and 103 degrees on Monday.
In Reno, Nev., maximum temperatures were expected to be about 84 degrees F Saturday and 81 degrees on Monday.
In the Pacific Northwest, forecasts for the weekend and early next week called for temperatures to average as much as five degrees above normal amid clouds and rain.
In Spokane, Wash, temperatures are expected to reach a high of 74 degrees on Saturday and 68 degrees on Monday.
Separately, Arizona Public Service's 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 1 nuclear power unit near Phoenix was expected to be back on line later Friday following a series of delays this week.
Also, the 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon nuclear power unit was expected to exit its refueling outage this weekend, a couple days later than originally expected.

Several other units were also expected to return to service by Monday, including a 750 MW unit at Colstrip in Montana, a 750 MW unit at Four Corners in Arizona, a 550 MW unit at Jim Bridger in Wyoming and a 400 MW unit at the Bonanza plant in Utah.
